shortDescription: Poland's manufacturing sector stabilised in October, ending nearly 18 months of contraction as exports rose and output broadly steadied, a business survey showed on Monday.

children: Poland's manufacturing sector stabilised in October, ending nearly 18 months of contraction as exports rose and output broadly steadied, a business survey showed on Monday.

The S&P Global Poland Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) rose to 50.0 in October from 49.0 in September. Analysts polled by Reuters had expected a reading of 49.4. A reading of exactly 50.0 signals no change in activity levels from the previous month.

"The latest upward movement in the headline figure reflected a slower decline in new orders, a near-stabilisation in output and higher employment," said Trevor Balchin, economics director at S&P Global Market Intelligence.
Total new business fell at the slowest rate since October 2025, while new export orders rose for the first time since last November.

Production was close to stabilising after four straight monthly declines, with the output sub-index at a five-month high and only fractionally below the 50.0 mark. Employment increased for the first time since July, though the pace of hiring was marginal.

Cost pressures intensified sharply. Input prices rose for a 12th straight month, with inflation climbing to its highest since June on higher raw material, transport and energy costs, while output price inflation eased slightly but stayed high.
Manufacturers remained optimistic that production would rise over the next 12 months, although confidence softened from September and backlogs of work fell for a ninth month.

title: Poland manufacturing holds steady in October for first time since April 2025, PMI shows
